newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade sharply ahead. [corrected 20:01 gmt]
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade sharply ahead. [corrected 20:01 gmt]

text.p: German shares surged ahead over a lively bourse session on Tuesday, propelled by overnight Wall Street gains and a recovery in the dollar that sparked renewed interest in the German share market, traders said.

The 30-share DAX index ended up 49 points, or 1.54 percent, at 3,233.21 points (corrects closing price from 3,223.21 points), while the IBIS DAX index was also stronger in early afternoon trade, up 49 points at 3,235.36 points.
"The friendly close on Wall Street is giving us some fresh energy," said one Frankfurt trader. "But I do not think many people are expecting a push the near-term to 3,300 points."
A lack of fresh corporate news kept the market focused on technical factors and a slew of German economic data.
The market generally ignored the 1.0 percent increase for January in German import prices -- gains due to the dollar -- for a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent.

Some traders said the reports from the states of Hesse and Baden-Wuerttemberg for February would prompt small hopes for a Bundesbank interest rate cut since the reports failed to spark worries of a sharp consumer price increase anytime soon.
"There are still hopes for a Bundesbank rate cut in the market but the dollar will be a hinderance," a trader said.
Among specific shares, insurance group Allianz AG Holding ended up 55 marks at 3,284 marks after its non-life insurance unit reported a profit of 1.607 billion marks, a 41.5 percent gain.

Airline Lufthansa ended bourse at 23 marks, unchanged from its closing level. The DAG union, which represents pilots and flight attendants, was expected on Wednesday to release the results of a strike authorisation ballot in a dispute over wage negotiations.
